## French Comments in devdesk — Reconnaissance Report

**Method:** ripgrep across all tracked `.go` files (no `vendor/`, `.worktrees/`, `node_modules` present in this repo). Two passes: (1) accented characters (`é è à ç ê ë î ô û ù â`) inside `//` comment lines, and (2) a broader pass adding unambiguous French function words (`des, une, sont, doit, doivent, cette, retourne, ...`), with ambiguous English/French homographs (`plus`, `part`, `comme`) deliberately excluded after they produced false positives. Both passes were spot-checked against string literals.

### Top-line numbers
- **119 files** contain at least one genuine French `//` comment line.
- **~2,030 French comment lines** total (1,659 of those carry an accented character; the remaining ~370 are accent-free French sentences/words caught only by the word-list pass, e.g. `main.go`'s `// Charger la configuration`).
- **Style note:** this codebase uses essentially **zero `/* */` block comments** (only 1 `/*` occurrence repo-wide) and **no `cmd/` directory at all** — everything lives under `internal/` plus a thin `main.go`. All French text is in `//` line comments (including multi-line `//` doc blocks).

### False positives checked
- Spot-checked accented-char hits inside string literals (test-table descriptions like `"loin de l'échéance"` in `internal/status/certificate_test.go`, and `Why:` UI-copy strings in `internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go:243-254`) — these are **real French text but NOT comments** (they're French strings shown/used at runtime or as test fixtures), correctly excluded from the comment count since they don't start with/contain a `//` prefix on those lines.
- The initial broad word-list pass falsely flagged ~75 extra files via `plus`/`part`/`comme` matching ordinary English comments (e.g. "the part", "plus the startup report"); removing those words dropped the false-positive set to 3 files, all of which were verified as genuinely containing a real (if short) French comment line elsewhere in the file (`internal/ui/forge/explorer/view.go:18` `// View rend la vue`, `internal/ui/security/header.go:158`, `internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:206`).

### Directory concentration
`internal/ui/` dominates overwhelmingly: **72 of 119 files** and **~1,528 of ~2,030 lines** (roughly 75% of both). Distant next tiers: `internal/metrics` (88 lines/5 files), `internal/app` (85/10), `internal/status` (70/8), `internal/command` (55/5), `internal/scan` (50/3), `internal/config` (48/1). Smaller tails in `internal/cache`, `internal/docker`, `internal/version`, `internal/credentials`, `main.go`, `internal/mcp`, `internal/shared`.

### Tests vs non-test files
French comments are **not** confined to production code — they show up in tests too:
- **32 of 119 files (27%)** are `_test.go` files, contributing **596 of ~2,030 lines (~29%)**.
- Non-test: 87 files, ~1,434 lines.
- Test files often carry the *rationale* for a test in French prose (e.g. `internal/command/doc_test.go`, `internal/ui/dashboard/posture_test.go`, `internal/ui/keymap/keymap_test.go`), same bilingual style as production code — not a different pattern, just as prevalent.

### Dense vs scattered
Two distinct patterns observed:
- **Dense, contiguous doc-block style** (whole package/function doc comment fully in French, with headers): `internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go` lines 1-~30 (`// Package keymap déclare le vocabulaire clavier...`, includes a French `# Trois espaces de noms disjoints` sub-heading) — this is the closest thing to a "pure French" block in the repo.
